A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEDDxAgent work. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original diagnostic evaluations on DDxPlus, iCraft-MD and RareBench, including component comparisons, simulated history taking and iterative diagnosis results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the main evaluations and appendix comparisons in Tables 4–8.

M1.justification: The DDxDriver, simulator, retrieval and diagnosis agents, and fixed/dynamic iteration procedures are unchanged. Section 2.4 adds an illustration of the existing dynamic scheduling behavior, without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three datasets, RareBench regional subsets, and complete-profile versus interactive diagnosis scenarios. The corrected demographics in a displayed DDxPlus example do not establish changed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged across the corresponding tables, including individual agents, history taking, retrieval and prompting variants, and UltraMedical models. Newly discussed CoD and MedAgentBench are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain 100 sampled patients per dataset, the same models and metrics, five few-shot examples, 5/10/15-question settings and one to three iterations. Section 4.2 clarifies the existing comparison configurations without changing their protocol.

E4.justification: Question-budget and iteration analyses, fixed-versus-dynamic comparisons, and existing diagnostic examples are retained. The added medical-model discussion interprets existing appendix results and supplies no new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: The fixed sampling-seed statement and point-estimate reporting remain unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the quoted DDxPlus zero-shot GTPA@1 baselines from 0.56 to 0.69 for GPT-4o and from 0.46 to 0.54 for Llama3.1-70B, matching the retained tables. The corresponding MEDDxAgent scores remain 0.86 and 0.71. All tabulated scores and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same metric definitions and average progress rate equation. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction adds public code availability as a fifth listed contribution. The scientific claims about modular interactive diagnosis, the three-domain benchmark, explainability and accuracy improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the explanation of medical-model underperformance, attributing it to specialized fine-tuning restricting general instruction following and describing retained results as confirmation. V2 also adds limitations concerning communication overhead, latency, computational cost and physician training against overreliance.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code statement and repository link. Its benchmark appendix corrects the DDxPlus example's initial age and sex from 41/F to 39/M, matching the full profile. Prompt templates and implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds five references, including CoD, MedAgentBench and work on general versus specialized medical models. Section 6.2 now explicitly recognizes CoD and MediQ as multi-turn history-taking frameworks; v1 grouped MediQ among approaches criticized for lacking iterative refinement.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, expands explanations in Sections 2.4 and 4.2, adds acknowledgments and renumbers the appendices following the architecture figure's relocation. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram moves from appendix Figure 4 to main-text Figure 2 with an expanded caption. The workflow example becomes Figure 3 with revised profile wording, and Table 1 gains an explicit GPT-4o heading. Existing charts and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reporting reliability by aligning Section 4.2 with Tables 1 and 7 and correcting the contradictory patient example. The code pointer, clearer architecture placement and added cost/deployment limitations improve usability and qualification. These are limited gains; the new causal explanation of medical-model underperformance is not established by the unchanged experiments.
